mainTopic: Notches in a שחיטה knife: which notches disqualify, how and by whom the knife is checked, and the shared measure of a chip
overview: A knife with many notches counts like a saw. With only one notch, an אוגרת notch makes the שחיטה invalid and a מסוכסכת notch leaves it valid. רבי אליעזר defines the two, and the גמרא narrows the case until מסוכסכת is fit only when the knife moved in one direction. רבא then sets out three levels of notch, and two reports of his view on מסוכסכת are reconciled by whether the knife went back and forth. רב אשי rules that a blade that is only slightly rough, like a grain bristle, is fully kosher. רב חסדא brings a פסוק for checking the knife, but the גמרא concludes that showing it to a חכם is only מדרבנן and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא. The גמרא lists ways to check a knife and disagrees over whether its three sides must be checked: רב פפא and the story with רב אשי say yes, while רב יימר says no because the cut opens wide. Finally, ריש לקיש lists three kinds of chips in holy animals, רב חסדא adds the knife, and all of them share the measure of a chip in the מזבח.

steps.title: Many notches versus one notch
steps.stepSummary: A knife with many notches is treated like a saw. With one notch, an אוגרת notch makes it unfit and a מסוכסכת notch leaves it fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A knife with many notches is judged like a saw. If it has only one notch: if the notch catches, the שחיטה is unfit; if it entangles, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the basic rule about a damaged knife used for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many notches turn the knife into a saw, which tears instead of cutting. With a single notch, it depends on the type of notch, אוגרת or מסוכסכת. Steps 2 and 3 explain what these two words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: A notch or nick in the blade
A saw, which tears instead of cutting smoothly
A notch that 'catches' and grabs the flesh
A notch that 'entangles' or rubs roughly

phrases.english: A knife that has many notches
is judged like a saw;
and one that has only one notch:
if it catches, it is unfit;
if it entangles, it is fit.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Many notches = like a saw. One notch: אוגרת is unfit, מסוכסכת is fit.

steps.title: What do the two kinds of notch look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to tell an אוגרת notch from a מסוכסכת notch.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a catching notch like? What is an entangling notch like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the two terms. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 gave opposite rulings for two kinds of notch, so we need to know exactly what each one is. Otherwise the rule cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? What is the case?

phrases.english: What is a catching notch like?
What is an entangling notch like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the terms used in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical difference between אוגרת and מסוכסכת

steps.title: Two sharp sides versus one sharp side
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says אוגרת has sharp edges on two sides and מסוכסכת on one side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: a catching notch is sharp on two sides; an entangling notch is sharp on one side.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question by describing the shape of each notch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A notch has two edges. If both are jagged it is אוגרת, which is unfit. If only one edge is jagged it is מסוכסכת, which is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Side or direction (here: an edge of the notch)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
A catching notch is one that is sharp on two sides;
an entangling notch is sharp on one side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹגֶרֶת מִשְׁתֵּי רוּחוֹת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אוגרת = jagged on two sides; מסוכסכת = jagged on one side

steps.title: Why should one sharp side be any better?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a one-sided notch can also cause damage in two stages, since the knife's tip weakens the neck and the notch then tears.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is two sides different? There, the first edge weakens and the second edge tears. With one side too, the sharp blade weakens and the notch's edge tears!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר's definition. It says the one-sided notch should be just as bad as the two-sided one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two jagged sides, the first edge weakens the neck and the second edge tears the סימנים. The גמרא argues that with one jagged side, the knife's own sharp blade does the weakening and the one jagged edge does the tearing. So the result looks the same.

keyTerms.meaning: A jagged edge of the notch
The sharp part of the blade

phrases.english: What is different about two sides,
that the first edge weakens
and the second edge tears?
With one side too,
the sharp part of the knife weakens,
and the edge of the notch tears!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's distinction between two sides and one side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The weaken-then-tear process also happens with a one-sided notch, so it should be unfit too

steps.title: The notch is at the tip of the knife
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is a notch at the very front of the knife, so no sharp blade comes before it to weaken the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a notch that stands at the front of the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by placing the notch at the start of the blade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the notch is at the very front, nothing sharp touches the neck before the notch does. So there is no weakening step, and the single jagged edge cannot tear.

keyTerms.meaning: The front end (head) of the knife

phrases.english: It is one that stands at the front of the knife.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any one-sided notch can weaken and then tear
steps.terutzMaskana: A notch at the front of the blade has no sharp blade before it, so it does not tear

steps.title: But the knife goes back and forth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even with the notch at the front, the blade weakens the neck going one way and the notch tears coming back.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when the knife goes it weakens, and when it comes back it tears!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the answer of step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering usually involves moving the knife both ways. On the return stroke the sharp blade has already weakened the neck, so the notch can tear after all.

phrases.english: In the end,
when it goes, it weakens,
when it comes back, it tears!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the notch is at the front of the knife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The back-and-forth motion still lets the blade weaken first and the notch tear afterward

steps.title: He moved the knife in one direction only
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is one where he moved the knife one way and did not bring it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he moved it one way and did not bring it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case again, so the kosher ruling for מסוכסכת holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no return stroke, the notch never meets a neck that was weakened first. So a one-sided notch stays fit only in this narrow case.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this line, מסוכסכת is fit only when the knife at the front was moved in one direction and not brought back.

phrases.english: For example, where he moved it one way and did not bring it back.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The knife always goes back and forth
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one stroke, so the notch never tears a weakened neck

steps.title: רבא's three levels of notch
steps.stepSummary: רבא lists three kinds of notch: אוגרת is unfit even after the fact; מסוכסכת should not be used at first but is valid after the fact; a smooth rising-and-falling notch may be used from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: there are three levels in a knife. If it catches, do not slaughter with it, and if he did, the שחיטה is unfit. If it entangles, do not slaughter with it at first, but if he did, the שחיטה is fit. If it rises and falls in the knife, one may slaughter with it from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a clear three-level ruling for a notched knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא adds a middle level. מסוכסכת is valid only after the fact (בדיעבד), not something to use לכתחילה. A notch that only rises and falls smoothly, with no jagged edges, is no problem at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Rises and falls (a smooth dip in the blade)

steps.whatToRemember: אוגרת is unfit even after the fact. מסוכסכת is valid only after the fact. A smooth 'rising and falling' blade is fine from the start.

phrases.english: Rava said: there are three levels in a knife:
if it catches, one may not slaughter,
and if he slaughtered, his slaughter is unfit.
If it entangles, one may not slaughter with it from the start,
but if he slaughtered, his slaughter is fit.
If it rises and falls in the knife,
phrases.notes: He means a smooth dip in the blade with no sharp, jagged edges.

phrases.english: one may slaughter with it from the start.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: אוגרת: unfit even after the fact; מסוכסכת: not at first, valid after the fact; עולה ויורד: allowed from the start
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-level list gives the practical rule for checking a שחיטה knife.

steps.title: Two opposite reports of רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נחמיה tells רב אשי that he once heard from him in רבא's name that מסוכסכת is unfit, but רבא said it is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נחמיה said to רב אשי: you told us in רבא's name that an entangling notch is unfit. But רבא said an entangling notch is fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between two statements reported in רבא's name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 has רבא saying מסוכסכת is valid after the fact. רב אשי had reported that רבא called it unfit. Both cannot be true unless they speak about different cases.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Nehemya said to Rav Ashi:
You told us in the name of Rava:
an entangling notch is unfit;
but Rava said: an entangling notch is fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחֶמְיָה לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two reports of רבא give opposite rulings for the same kind of notch

steps.title: It depends on back-and-forth
steps.stepSummary: The answer: unfit when he moved the knife back and forth; fit when he moved it one way only.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, where he moved it one way and back; there, where he moved it one way and did not bring it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is solved by placing each report of רבא in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches steps 6 and 7. With a back-and-forth stroke, the blade weakens and the notch tears, so מסוכסכת is unfit. With a single stroke it stays fit.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there (each ruling is for a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: מסוכסכת is unfit if the knife went back and forth, and fit if it went one way only.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא changed his mind. Both reports are correct, each for a different way of moving the knife.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, where he moved it one way and brought it back;
phrases.notes: This is the case where רבא said it is unfit.

phrases.english: there, where he moved it one way and did not bring it back.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of רבא contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Unfit with back-and-forth; fit with one stroke only

steps.title: What about a knife that feels like a grain stalk?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks רב אשי about a knife that is slightly rough, like the bristle of a grain stalk, but has no real notch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב אויא, asked רב אשי: if the knife is like a grain bristle, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: After רבא's three kinds of notch, a new case is raised: a blade that is a little rough but has no actual notch. The question sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's list covered blades with real notches. This blade sits below even the mildest notch, so the question is whether such slight roughness counts as a problem at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The bristle of a grain stalk. It feels slightly rough but has no real gaps.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:
If it is like a grain bristle, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "It" is the knife's blade: slightly rough, but with no real notch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a borderline case below רבא's categories of notch.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a knife with slight roughness but no real notch valid for שחיטה?

steps.title: Such a knife is completely fine
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that he would happily eat meat slaughtered with such a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who will give us some of its meat so we can eat it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that a grain-bristle knife is fully kosher. He says it so strongly that he wishes someone would give him the meat to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer is a vivid way of saying there is no doubt at all. Slight roughness is not a notch, so it does not tear the neck and does not cause a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will give us? Here it means 'If only someone would give us!'

steps.whatToRemember: A blade that is only slightly rough, like a grain bristle, is completely valid for שחיטה.

phrases.english: He said to him: Who will give us
some of its meat, so that we may eat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the grain-bristle knife.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The knife is fully valid; meat slaughtered with it may be eaten without hesitation.

steps.title: A Torah source for checking the knife
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the duty to check the knife comes from the Torah, based on a פסוק about שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: From where do we know that checking the knife is from the Torah? As it says: 'And slaughter with this and eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא opens a new topic: where the requirement to check a שחיטה knife comes from. He brings a פסוק from the story of שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'with this' points to a specific knife that was ready to use. רב חסדא reads it as showing that the knife has to be checked before שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking the knife for notches before שחיטה
From the Torah itself, not only a rabbinic rule

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
From where do we know that checking a knife is from the Torah?
As it says: "And slaughter with this and eat."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 14:34. "With this" is read as a specific knife that had already been checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the source for checking the knife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking a knife is a Torah requirement, learned from "וּשְׁחַטְתֶּם בָּזֶה וַאֲכַלְתֶּם".

steps.title: Isn't checking the knife obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed. A notch would make the animal a טריפה, so of course the knife must be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! Since a hole would make it a טריפה, it needs checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. Common sense already tells us to check the knife, so why bring a פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A notched knife can tear a hole in the food pipe, and a hole there makes the animal a טריפה. Since we already know we must check, a special source looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! Used to ask why something even needs saying.
He made a hole (in the food pipe)
An animal with a fatal defect, so it may not be eaten

phrases.english: It is obvious! Since if he made a hole, it is a tereifa,
it needs checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב חסדא's source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's need for a פסוק to require checking the knife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Logic alone requires checking, because a notch would make the animal a טריפה. So a פסוק is unnecessary.

steps.title: The source is for showing the knife to a חכם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא's source is for showing the knife to a חכם, not just for checking it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about showing it to a חכם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב חסדא really meant. The פסוק teaches that the knife must be shown to a חכם for checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Basic checking is obvious, but the extra step of bringing the knife to a חכם is not. In the story, שאול (the leader) handed over a knife he had prepared, so the פסוק fits showing it to a leader or חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: We are saying, or we are talking about

phrases.english: We are speaking about showing it to a scholar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing what רב חסדא meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא was giving a source for basic checking, which is obvious anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא was giving a source for showing the knife to a חכם.

steps.title: Showing the knife to a חכם is only for his honor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from רבי יוחנן, who said showing the knife to a חכם is only out of respect for the חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: They only said to show the knife to a חכם because of the honor of the חכם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. רבי יוחנן says showing the knife to a חכם is just a matter of respect, so how can it be a Torah law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's words 'they said' point to a rule the rabbis made, and his reason is honor, not a Torah need. That clashes with calling it מן התורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor and respect due to a Torah scholar

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
They only said to show a knife to a scholar
because of the honor of the scholar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer that the source is for showing the knife to a חכם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that showing the knife to a חכם is a Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says this rule exists only out of respect for the חכם, which sounds rabbinic, not from the Torah.

steps.title: It is rabbinic and the פסוק is only a support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that showing the knife to a חכם is מדרבנן, and the פסוק is only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is from the rabbis, and the פסוק is just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבי יוחנן's view. The rule is rabbinic, and רב חסדא's פסוק is only a hint the rabbis attached to their rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So רב חסדא's 'from the Torah' is not taken literally. The פסוק does not create the law. It is a support connected to a rule the rabbis made to honor חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: From the rabbis, a rabbinic law
Just a support: a פסוק used as a hint for a rabbinic rule, not as its real source

steps.whatToRemember: Checking the knife is obviously needed. Showing it to a חכם is only מדרבנן, out of respect, and the פסוק is just an אסמכתא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב חסדא's פסוק makes showing the knife a Torah law. The גמרא concludes it is only an אסמכתא for a rabbinic rule.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי יוחנן's challenge by downgrading the פסוק to a support.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source as an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Showing the knife to a חכם is a Torah law learned from the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a rabbinic law for the חכם's honor, and the פסוק is only a support.

steps.title: Different ways to check a knife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists how knives were checked: in the sun, with water, with the tip of the tongue, or with a hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they check it in the sun. In נהרדעא they check it with water. רב ששת checked it with the tip of his tongue. רב אחא בר יעקב checked it with a strand of hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds practical information: the different methods people used to find notches in a knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each method is a different way to notice a tiny notch. Sunlight can show it, water moves around it, the tongue can feel it, and a hair catches in it. All of them aim at the same goal: a smooth blade.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
With the tip of his tongue

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the goal is finding even a tiny notch. Any reliable method that does this is a valid way to check.

phrases.english: In the West they check it in the sun,
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which is west of Bavel.

phrases.english: in Neharde'a they check it with water,

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת בָּדֵק לַהּ בְּרֵישׁ לִישָּׁנֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet would check it with the tip of his tongue,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב בָּדֵק לַהּ בְּחוּט הַשַּׂעֲרָה.
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov would check it with a strand of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the duty to check comes from to how the check is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife may be checked by sunlight, water, the tip of the tongue, or a strand of hair.

steps.title: In סורא: test the knife on flesh
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of סורא say that since the knife cuts flesh, it should be checked on flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא they say: the knife eats flesh, so let flesh check it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more method of checking the knife. The scholars of סורא say to test it on your own flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is simple: the worry is that a notch will tear the flesh of the animal. So the best test is to run the blade over flesh and feel whether it catches.

keyTerms.meaning: A major Torah center in בבל

phrases.english: In Sura they say:
It eats flesh; let flesh examine it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the knife. Since it cuts flesh, you check it against flesh, like your fingertip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another method of checking, after the list in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knife should be checked against flesh, because flesh is what it cuts.

steps.title: רב פפא: three checks are needed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the knife must be checked on the flesh, on the fingernail, and on all three sides of the blade.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the knife needs checking on the flesh, on the fingernail, and on its three sides.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a fuller rule for checking the knife. He requires three kinds of checks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flesh and fingernail are two different tests, and each can catch a notch the other might miss. The "three sides" are the sharp edge plus the two flat sides of the blade, so even the sides must be free of notches.

keyTerms.meaning: Three sides: the sharp edge and the two flat sides of the blade

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It requires examination on the flesh,
and on the fingernail, and on the three sides.
phrases.notes: The three sides are the sharp edge and the two flat sides next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the flesh test from step 19 into a fuller three-part check.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The knife must be checked on flesh, on the fingernail, and on all three sides.

steps.title: רבינא asks רב אשי about a report in his name
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב אשי that רב סמא reported in רב אשי's name, quoting רבא, that all three checks are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: רב סמא son of רב משרשיא told us in your name that you told him in the name of רבא: the knife needs checking on the flesh, the fingernail, and the three sides.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא checks a report with רב אשי directly. He wants to know if רב אשי really said this, and in רבא's name. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about who said what. It matters because a ruling coming from רבא carries more weight. The answer will show which part of the ruling is reliable.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of (quoting someone else)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לַן רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא מִשְּׁמָךְ,
phrases.english: Rav Sama son of Rav Mesharshiyya told us in your name
that you told him in the name of Rava:
It requires examination on the flesh
and on the fingernail and on the three sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks who really said the three-part rule from step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רב אשי really say all three checks are needed, and in the name of רבא?

steps.title: רב אשי: I did not say the three sides
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that he said to check on flesh and fingernail, but not the three sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I said on the flesh and on the fingernail, but I did not say on the three sides.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי corrects the report. He agrees to two of the checks but denies saying the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the part of the rule that was added by mistake is the three sides. So according to this version, רב אשי only requires flesh and fingernail.

phrases.english: He said to him:
On the flesh and on the fingernail I said;
and on the three sides I did not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי said flesh and fingernail, not the three sides.

steps.title: Another version: all three, but not from רבא
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב אשי answered that he did say all three checks, but not in the name of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he answered: I said on the flesh, the fingernail, and the three sides, but I did not say it in the name of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב אשי's answer. Here the mistake is only about whose name it was said in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the rule itself is right: all three checks are needed. What was wrong is only the claim that it came from רבא; it was רב אשי's own view.
steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree רב אשי was misquoted. They disagree about what the mistake was: the three sides (step 22) or the name of רבא (this step).

phrases.english: There are those who say:
On the flesh and on the fingernail and on the three sides I said;
in the name of Rava I did not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי did require all three checks, but as his own view, not in the name of רבא.

steps.title: רב אשי approves checking all three sides
steps.stepSummary: A knife was brought to רב אשי. רב אחא checked it on the nail, the flesh, and the three sides, and רב אשי praised him and quoted רב כהנא as agreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא and רב אחא son of רבא were sitting before רב אשי. A knife was brought to רב אשי to be checked. He told רב אחא son of רבא: check it. He checked it on the fingernail, the flesh, and the three sides. רב אשי said: well done, and רב כהנא said the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how רב אשי acted in practice. He approved checking all three sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story fits the second version (step 23), where רב אשי does require the three sides. It also adds רב כהנא as another authority who holds this way.

phrases.english: Ravina and Rav Aḥa son of Rava
were sitting before Rav Ashi.

phrases.aramaic: אַיְיתוֹ סַכִּין לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי לִבְדְּקַהּ.
phrases.english: They brought a knife before Rav Ashi to examine it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: בִּידְקַהּ.
phrases.english: He said to Rav Aḥa son of Rava: Examine it.
He examined it on the fingernail and on the flesh and on the three sides.
He said to him: Well done,
and so said Rav Kahana.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא וְרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice that רב אשי approved checking the three sides.
steps.raayaObject: That the three sides of the knife should be checked.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's approval of רב אחא's check, plus רב כהנא's agreement.

steps.title: רב יימר: the sides don't need checking
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר says checking on the fingernail and flesh is needed, but checking the three sides is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: the fingernail and the flesh are needed; the three sides are not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר disagrees with requiring the three sides. The גמרא will next bring a proof for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יימר keeps the two main checks but drops the sides. His idea is that only the cutting edge matters, because the sides never really touch the neck in a way that tears.

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said:
On the fingernail and on the flesh is necessary;
on the three sides is not necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב פפא and the story about רב אשי on the three sides.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only fingernail and flesh checks are required, not the three sides.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל's red-hot knife
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר brings שמואל's ruling that שחיטה with a red-hot knife is valid. The question was asked that the hot sides should burn the neck, and the answer was that the cut opens wide right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי זירא say in the name of שמואל: if someone heated a knife until it was white-hot and did שחיטה with it, the שחיטה is valid, because the sharp edge cuts before the heat burns. And we asked: but what about the sides of the knife? And we answered: the place of the cut opens wide.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר proves his view from an earlier ruling about a red-hot knife. That ruling already showed that the sides of a knife don't touch the cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the red-hot case, the worry was that the hot sides would burn the neck and make the animal a טריפה. The answer was that the cut opens apart right away, so the sides don't touch. That same idea will now be used for notches on the sides.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of the cut on the neck

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Zeira say that Shmuel said:
If one heated a knife white-hot and slaughtered with it,
his slaughter is valid,
because its sharpness comes before its heat;
and it was difficult for us: But there are the sides!
phrases.notes: The hot flat sides should still burn the neck as the knife passes through.

phrases.english: And we said: The place of slaughter opens wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support רב יימר in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That the sides of the knife don't touch the cut, so they need no checking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling on a red-hot knife and the explanation that the cut opens wide.

steps.title: Same here: the cut opens, so the sides don't matter
steps.stepSummary: Just as with the red-hot knife, the cut opens wide, so notches on the sides never touch the סימנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the place of the cut opens wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the red-hot knife idea to our case. This finishes רב יימר's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sides can't burn the neck because the cut opens, they also can't tear it with a notch. So according to רב יימר, there's no need to check the three sides.
steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא (and the story with רב אשי) say to check the knife on flesh, fingernail, and all three sides. רב יימר says only flesh and fingernail, because the cut opens wide and the sides never touch it.

phrases.english: Here too,
the place of slaughter opens wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה מִרְוָוח רָוַוח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer from the red-hot knife case in step 26 to the question of checking the sides.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רב יימר, the sides of the knife don't need checking, because the cut opens and the sides never touch the סימנים.

steps.title: Three kinds of chips that matter
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש lists three cases where a small chip has legal weight: a bone of the קרבן פסח, the ear of a בכור, and a מום in קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר רב קטינא said in the name of ריש לקיש: There are three kinds of chips: a chip in a bone of the קרבן פסח, a chip in the ear of a בכור, and a chip that counts as a מום in קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new statement listing three kinds of 'chips' (פגימות) that matter in הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is about holy animals. Breaking a bone of the פסח is forbidden, a chipped ear makes a בכור blemished, and a chip can be a מום that disqualifies other קרבנות. The list groups them together because, as the גמרא will say, they share one measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The Passover offering, whose bones may not be broken
A firstborn animal, given to the כהן
A blemish that makes an animal unfit to be a קרבן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina said
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
There are three kinds of chips:
a chip in a bone of the Pesach offering,
a chip in the ear of a firstborn animal,
and a chip that is a blemish in holy offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement that groups together different kinds of chips, connecting to the earlier talk about nicks in a knife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three kinds of chips matter: a bone of the פסח, the ear of a בכור, and a מום in קדשים.

steps.title: Adding a nick in the knife
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds a fourth item to the list: a nick in a שחיטה knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Also a nick in a knife.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds the knife used for שחיטה as a fourth kind of chip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties the list back to the topic of the סוגיא, checking a knife for nicks. A nick in the knife also has legal weight, since it can make the שחיטה invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: A nick in the knife used for שחיטה

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Also a nick in a knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אַף פְּגִימַת סַכִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth item to ריש לקיש's list of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nick in a שחיטה knife belongs on the list too.

steps.title: Why the knife was left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that ריש לקיש did not mention the knife because he was only talking about holy animals, not חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (ריש לקיש) was not talking about regular, non-holy animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש did not include the knife in his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three of ריש לקיש's cases are about קדשים. A שחיטה knife is used for regular חולין too, so it did not fit his list. This means he does not really disagree with רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument between them. ריש לקיש would agree a knife's nick matters; he just limited his list to holy animals.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Meaning ריש לקיש: why didn't he list the knife?

phrases.english: He is not talking about non-holy animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the gap between ריש לקיש's list of three and רב חסדא's added fourth.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's list, which leaves out the knife
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the list was only about קדשים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think ריש לקיש holds that a knife's nick does not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: He simply was not speaking about חולין, where the knife belongs.

steps.title: All share the altar's measure
steps.stepSummary: All these chips are measured by the same size as a chip that makes the מזבח unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all of them, the size of their chip is the same as the chip size of the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא continues his statement and gives one shared size for all the chips on the list, including the knife he added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why the cases were grouped together: they all use one measure. That measure is borrowed from the rule of a chipped מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The amount of, the same size as
The altar in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: There are four kinds of chips (פסח bone, בכור ear, מום in קדשים, and a שחיטה knife), and all use the same size as a chip in the מזבח.

phrases.english: And all of them, their chip
is the same as the chip of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the shared measure that ties the whole list together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed chips are measured by the size of a chip that disqualifies the מזבח.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One size, the מזבח's, defines a meaningful chip in all four cases.
